elements.text: Fire of undetermined origin
Underestimate of fire severity by the captain
Misleading fire progress information provided to the captain
Time taken to evaluate the nature of the fire and decide to initiate an emergency descent
Delayed decision to descend and land
Fire propagated through amenities section and burned undetected for almost 15 minutes
Flightcrew did not consider simultaneous tripping of flush motor circuit breakers a serious problem
Captain was not informed of precise location and extent of the fire
Crewmember report that fire was abating misled captain about severity
Loss of air conditioning and pressurization packs accelerated accumulation of smoke, heat, and toxic gases
Passing out wet towels and instructing passengers to breathe through them aided survival
Opening of overwing exit windows by passengers
Flashfire occurred after doors and exits were opened
Airplane was registered, equipped, and maintained in accordance with regulations
Flightcrew and cabin crew were qualified and trained
Fire was not set deliberately nor result of explosive/incendiary device
Safety Board could not identify origin of fire
Faulty ATC handoff did not significantly delay landing
This was a survivable accident
Investigation and public hearing details
